verdicts.quote: Endpoint `POST /tickets/:id/merge`, body `{ "into": "T-0001" }` ... 200 with the duplicate ticket ... or an unknown field is 400 `invalid`.
(`:id` is the duplicate, `into` the surviving ticket).
Order of checks (first failure wins): request body 400; unknown `:id` 404; unknown `into` 404; self-merge 409; closed duplicate 409; closed target 409.
verdicts.missing: The spec never says outright whether the tickets must look alike (same requester, title or priority) or whether the agent's say-so is enough. That can only be inferred from the list of checks.

verdicts.quote: now `status: "closed"` and `mergedInto: "<into>"` ... Invariant: a ticket with `mergedInto` is `closed` and the target exists.
verdicts.missing: The spec does not say whether a merged ticket can later be edited, transitioned or reopened, or what answer such an attempt gets.

verdicts.quote: The surviving ticket is unchanged (title, priority, status, `updated`). ... the survivor's own fields and `updated` stay as they were
`GET /tickets/:id` of a merged ticket still answers. ... the weekly report and `GET /tickets?status=closed` count a merged ticket as closed.
Failure (409 `conflict`, message names the reason): merging a ticket into itself; a duplicate that is already closed (including already merged); a surviving ticket that is closed.
verdicts.missing: The spec does not say what happens when either ticket is resolved (or in any other non-closed, non-open status).

verdicts.quote: unknown `:id` or unknown `into` is 404 `not_found`; body not an object, missing or non-ticket-id `into`, or an unknown field is 400 `invalid`.
verdicts.missing: The status codes are given, but not which id the error message names.

verdicts.quote: chains are allowed and not flattened ... Cycles cannot occur because a merged ticket is closed and a closed ticket is refused as a target.
a duplicate that is already closed (including already merged) [409] ... A refused merge changes nothing: no audit entry, no notification, no save.
the surviving ticket gets one entry, action `ticket.merge_received` ... the survivor's own fields and `updated` stay as they were
any caller naming itself in `X-Actor` (default `system`) may merge ... no authentication or role check is added
a merged ticket reloads with `status`, `mergedInto` ... `version` stays 1; a data file written before this change loads unchanged (no `mergedInto` means not merged)
a record whose `mergedInto` is present but is not a ticket id, is its own id, names no ticket in the file, or sits on a ticket that is not `closed` is refused as a corrupt data file
verdicts.missing: The spec does not say that the refusal message names the offending record. It also does not say whether cycles longer than one ticket in the file (A into B, B into A) are detected.

verdicts.quote: one audit entry on the duplicate, action `ticket.merged`, the request's actor, changes `{ status: {from, to: "closed"}, mergedInto: ...}`; the surviving ticket gets one entry, action `ticket.merge_received`
a merge is applied atomically in memory (both tickets and the audit entries change in one store call, then one save)
verdicts.missing: The spec does not say whether the outbox notification belongs to the same atomic change. It also does not say that a crash must leave the state either before or after the merge.

verdicts.quote: one `ticket.merged` outbox notification to the duplicate's requester, key `ticket.merged:<id>` ... the surviving ticket's requester is not notified
verdicts.missing: The spec does not say what happens to notifications about the absorbed ticket that are still pending.

verdicts.quote: The operators' CLI stays read-only: `show` prints a merged ticket normally, with one extra detail line ... label `merged into` ... `list` and `list --raw` columns are unchanged
Preserved: all existing endpoints, ticket fields and lifecycle ... `mergedInto` is present only on a merged ticket (absent, not null, on every other ticket, so existing ticket bodies are unchanged).
`list` and `list --raw` columns are unchanged (the weekly report reads them by position). ... the weekly report ... count a merged ticket as closed.
`CHANGELOG.md` gains a 1.5.0 section and `package.json` version 1.5.0 ... a decision record (docs/decisions/0009) ... Dependencies: none added
verdicts.missing: The spec does not require a test for atomicity. It also does not explicitly require the change to be made through a TicketStore method; it only says "one store call".
